claim: Regulation of RNA polymerase II (Pol2) elongation in the promoter-proximal region is an important and ubiquitous control point for gene expression in metazoans.
source: Regulation of RNA polymerase II (Pol2) elongation in the promoter-proximal region is an important and ubiquitous control point for gene expression in metazoans.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge about transcriptional regulation in metazoans.

claim: Transcription of the adenovirus 5 E4 region is regulated during the release of paused Pol2 into productive elongation by recruitment of the super-elongation complex, dependent on promoter H3K18/27 acetylation by CBP/p300.
source: We report that transcription of the adenovirus 5 E4 region is regulated during the release of paused Pol2 into productive elongation by recruitment of the super-elongation complex, dependent on promoter H3K18/27 acetylation by CBP/p300.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data including GRO-seq and ChIP-seq analyses.

claim: This transcriptional regulatory mechanism applies to approximately 7% of expressed protein-coding genes in primary human airway epithelial cells.
source: We also establish that this is a general transcriptional regulatory mechanism that applies to ~7% of expressed protein-coding genes in primary human airway epithelial cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by genome-wide analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: A homeostatic mechanism maintains promoter, but not enhancer, H3K18/27ac in response to extensive inhibition of CBP/p300 acetyl transferase activity by A-485.
source: We observed that a homeostatic mechanism maintains promoter, but not enhancer, H3K18/27ac in response to extensive inhibition of CBP/p300 acetyl transferase activity by the highly specific small molecule inhibitor A-485.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data showing differential effects of A-485 on promoters versus enhancers.

claim: BRD4 association at enhancers regulates paused Pol2 release at nearby promoters.
source: Further, our results suggest a function for BRD4 association at enhancers in regulating paused Pol2 release at nearby promoters.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from correlative data showing relationships between BRD4 enhancer binding and Pol2 pausing at nearby genes.

claim: After recruitment of Pol2 to a promoter, transcription initiation occurs concurrently with TFIIH phosphorylation of Ser5 of the Pol2 heptapeptide repeat C-terminal domain (CTD).
source: After the recruitment of Pol2 to a promoter by its general transcription factors and assembly of a PIC (Nogales et al., 2017; Sainsbury et al., 2015), transcription initiation occurs concurrently with TFIIH phosphorylation of Ser5 of the Pol2 heptapeptide repeat C-terminal domain (CTD) (Cramer, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: In metazoan cells, Pol2 transcribes approximately 30–60 bases downstream of the transcription start site (TSS) and then pauses because it is bound by NELF and DSIF.
source: In metazoan cells, Pol2 then transcribes approximately 30–60 bases downstream of the transcription start site (TSS) and then pauses because it is bound by negative elongation factor (NELF) and DRB-sensitivity-inducing factor (DSIF, Spt4 and Spt5 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae) (Jonkers and Lis, 2015; Adelman and Lis, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Association of elongation factor P-TEFb results in phosphorylation of NELF, DSIF, and Ser2 of the Pol2 CTD, whereupon NELF dissociates and Pol2 is released and proceeds to productive elongation.
source: Association of elongation factor P-TEFb, including its enzymatic subunits CDK9-cyclin T, results in phosphorylation of NELF, DSIF, and Ser2 of the Pol2 CTD, whereupon NELF dissociates and Pol2 is released and proceeds to productive elongation (Cramer, 2019; Jonkers and Lis, 2015; Adelman and Lis, 2012; Vos et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Histone acetylation contributes to a permissive chromatin state for Pol2 PIC assembly at active promoters.
source: Histone acetylation is well known to contribute to a permissive chromatin state for Pol2 PIC assembly at active promoters, and there is recently published work concerning its function in facilitating transcriptional elongation as well.
evidence: This claim is supported by established scientific knowledge.

claim: BRD4 is thought to recruit P-TEFb (CDK9-cyclin T) to promoters and serves as a Pol2 elongation factor dependent on its interactions with acetylated histone lysines through its bromodomains.
source: For example, the chromatin reader protein BRD4 is thought to recruit P-TEFb (CDK9-cyclin T) to promoters and serves as a Pol2 elongation factor dependent on its interactions with acetylated histone lysines through its bromodomains (Kanno et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: H3 acetylation mediated by the Drosophila CBP ortholog stimulates productive elongation past the +1 nucleosome.
source: In addition, H3 acetylation mediated by the Drosophila CBP ortholog stimulates productive elongation past the +1 nucleosome (Boija et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Recruitment of the yeast histone chaperone FACT by acetylated H3 stimulates elongation.
source: Recruitment of the yeast histone chaperone FACT by acetylated H3 has also been shown to stimulate elongation (Pathak et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The super-elongation complex (SEC) comprises P-TEFb (CDK9-cyclin T) along with AF4/FMR2 proteins AFF1/4, ELL family members ELL1/2/3, ELL-associated factors EAF1/2, and AF9 or ENL containing YEATS acetyl-lysine-binding domains.
source: The super-elongation complex (SEC) is a multi-subunit complex comprising P-TEFb (CDK9-cyclin T) along with AF4/FMR2 proteins AFF1/4, ELL family members ELL1/2/3, ELL-associated factors EAF1/2, and one or the other highly homologous proteins AF9 or ENL containing YEATS acetyl-lysine-binding domains (Luo et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: ENL and AF9 have been functionally linked to SEC recruitment to acetylated chromatin via their YEATS domains.
source: ENL and AF9 have been functionally linked to SEC recruitment to acetylated chromatin via their YEATS domains (Li et al., 2014; Gates et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: AF9 and ENL YEATS domains bind to active chromatin marks H3K9ac and H4K15ac, and to a lesser extent H3K18/27ac.
source: Importantly, AF9 and ENL YEATS domains bind to active chromatin marks H3K9ac and H4K15ac (Gates et al., 2017), and, to a lesser extent, H3K18/27ac (Li et al., 2014), and are essential for SEC-dependent activation of a luciferase reporter driven by the HIV-1 LTR (He et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: CBP/p300 acetylation of H3K18 and K27 in the two to three nucleosomes spanning the TSS had very different effects on distinct steps in transcription from different human adenovirus 5 (HAdV-5) early promoters.
source: We previously reported that CBP/p300 acetylation of H3K18 and K27 in the two to three nucleosomes spanning the TSS had very different effects on distinct steps in transcription from different human adenovirus 5 (HAdV-5) early promoters (Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: At the E3 promoter, loss of H3K18/27ac in the promoter region had little effect on PIC assembly, and the rate of E3 mRNA synthesis was only modestly reduced (less than twofold) compared to transcription activated by wt E1A.
source: At the E3 promoter, loss of H3K18/27ac in the promoter region had little effect on PIC assembly, and the rate of E3 mRNA synthesis was only modestly reduced (less than twofold) compared to transcription activated by wt E1A, which induces H3K18/27ac at the early viral promoters.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: PIC assembly at the E2early promoter was almost eliminated by loss of promoter H3K18/27ac, and E2 mRNA synthesis was undetectable at 12 hr post-infection.
source: In contrast, PIC assembly at the E2early promoter was almost eliminated by loss of promoter H3K18/27ac, and E2 mRNA synthesis was undetectable at 12 hr post-infection (p.i.) (Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: For E4, loss of promoter H3K18/27ac had little effect on PIC assembly but caused a significant (approximately tenfold) decrease in E4 transcription at 12 hr p.i.
source: For E4, loss of promoter H3K18/27ac had little effect on PIC assembly but caused a significant (approximately tenfold) decrease in E4 transcription at 12 hr p.i. (Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work by the authors.

claim: The E4 transcription result suggests that E4 transcription is regulated by promoter H3K18/27 acetylation at a step in transcription subsequent to PIC assembly, possibly during release of promoter-proximal paused Pol2.
source: This result was particularly striking as it suggested that E4 transcription is regulated by promoter H3K18/27 acetylation at a step in transcription subsequent to PIC assembly, possibly during release of promoter-proximal paused Pol2.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the observation that PIC assembly was not affected but transcription was reduced.

claim: The E4 pausing index increased 2.5-fold on average in three biological replicate GRO-seq experiments when activated by DM-E1A compared to wt E1A.
source: After activation by DM-E1A, the PI at E4 increased 2.5-fold on average in three biological replicate GRO-seq experiments, a significant increase compared to the degree of pausing at E4 when activated by wt E1A (Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRO-seq experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: There was no significant change in pausing index at E3 where promoter H3K18/27 acetylation had only a modest effect on transcription.
source: In contrast to E4, there was no significant change in PI at E3 where promoter H3K18/27 acetylation had only a modest effect on transcription (Hsu et al., 2018; Figure 1b).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRO-seq data shown in Figure 1b and citation to prior work.

claim: The low level of GRO-seq counts at the E2early promoter region showed an insignificant change in PI between wt E1A and DM E1A.
source: Similar to E3, the low level of GRO-seq counts at the E2early promoter region showed an insignificant change in PI between wt E1A and DM E1A (Figure 1b), suggesting that H3K18/27ac acetylation does not affect pause release at the E2early promoter and primarily promotes Pol2 initiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by GRO-seq data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: H3K18/27ac acetylation does not affect pause release at the E2early promoter and primarily promotes Pol2 initiation.
source: Similar to E3, the low level of GRO-seq counts at the E2early promoter region showed an insignificant change in PI between wt E1A and DM E1A (Figure 1b), suggesting that H3K18/27ac acetylation does not affect pause release at the E2early promoter and primarily promotes Pol2 initiation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the GRO-seq data.

claim: Loss of H3K18/27 promoter acetylation produced a smaller defect on promoter-proximal Pol2 pause release at the E2 and E3 promoters than at the E4 promoter.
source: Therefore, loss of H3K18/27 promoter acetylation produced a smaller defect on promoter-proximal Pol2 pause release at the E2 and E3 promoters than at the E4 promoter.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the comparative GRO-seq data for E2, E3, and E4.

claim: The CDK7 subunit of TFIIH phosphorylates Ser5 of the Pol2 CTD repeat during transcription initiation.
source: The CDK7 subunit of TFIIH phosphorylates Ser5 of the Pol2 CTD repeat during transcription initiation, and subsequently the CDK9 subunit of P-TEFb phosphorylates Ser2 of the CTD repeat, NELF, and DSIF causing release of Pol2 arrested by NELF binding in the promoter-proximal region, and the transition to productive elongation (Cramer, 2019; Jonkers and Lis, 2015; Rahl et al., 2010; Yamada et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The CDK9 subunit of P-TEFb phosphorylates Ser2 of the CTD repeat, NELF, and DSIF causing release of Pol2 arrested by NELF binding in the promoter-proximal region, and the transition to productive elongation.
source: The CDK7 subunit of TFIIH phosphorylates Ser5 of the Pol2 CTD repeat during transcription initiation, and subsequently the CDK9 subunit of P-TEFb phosphorylates Ser2 of the CTD repeat, NELF, and DSIF causing release of Pol2 arrested by NELF binding in the promoter-proximal region, and the transition to productive elongation (Cramer, 2019; Jonkers and Lis, 2015; Rahl et al., 2010; Yamada et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: At E2early, Ser5-P peaked near the TSS and decreased throughout the gene body, a distribution that is typical in yeast and mouse ES cells.
source: At E2early, Ser5-P peaked near the TSS and decreased throughout the gene body, a distribution that is typical in yeast that also has short genes with few introns (Buratowski, 2009), as well as mouse ES cells (Rahl et al., 2010) with the much longer, multi-exon, long-intron genes typical of vertebrates.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2a and citations to prior literature.

claim: Two Ser2-P peaks were observed in the E2early gene body, one positioned just downstream of the TSS probably corresponding to paused Pol2 in complex with NELF, and a second peak upstream of the E2early second exon.
source: We observed two Ser2-P peaks in the E2early gene body, one positioned just downstream of the TSS probably corresponding to paused Pol2 in complex with NELF, and a second peak upstream of the E2early second exon.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Pol2 peaks just upstream of the E2 second exon may be explained by a previously reported reduction in elongation rate over some exons, proposed to influence splice site recognition and spliceosome assembly.
source: These Pol2 peaks just upstream of the E2 second exon may be explained by a previously reported reduction in elongation rate over some exons, proposed to influence splice site recognition and spliceosome assembly (Jonkers et al., 2014; Martin et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the data and citations to prior literature.

claim: Both CDK9 and NELF peaks occurred at the expected E2early, E3, and E4 pause sites approximately 40 bp downstream of the TSSs.
source: Both CDK9 and NELF peaks occurred at the expected E2early, E3, and E4 pause sites ~40 bp downstream of the TSSs (Figure 2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Broad enrichment of Ser2-P and Ser5-P Pol2 was observed downstream of the E3 and E4 poly(A) sites.
source: Broad enrichment of Ser2-P and Ser5-P Pol2 was also observed downstream of the E3 and E4 poly(A) sites.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Increased Pol2 Ser2-P and Ser5-P downstream from cellular poly(A) sites is observed at most genes in mammalian cells and is thought to result from a decrease in Pol2 elongation rate following nascent RNA cleavage at the poly(A) site.
source: Increased Pol2 Ser2-P and Ser5-P downstream from cellular poly(A) sites is observed at most genes in mammalian cells and is thought to result from a decrease in Pol2 elongation rate following nascent RNA cleavage at the poly(A) site (Rahl et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Reduced H3K18/27ac in DM-E1A vector-infected cells compared to wt E1A-expressing cells correlated with decreased CDK9, AF9, and ENL association with the viral early promoters and gene bodies.
source: Reduced H3K18/27ac in DM-E1A vector-infected cells compared to wt E1A-expressing cells correlated with decreased CDK9, AF9, and ENL association with the viral early promoters and gene bodies compared to cells expressing wt E1A (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: There was no decrease in average AF9 and ENL association with TSSs of most human genes in cells expressing DM-E1A, demonstrating the specificity of this effect on SEC subunit association at the viral early promoters.
source: Importantly, we did not observe decreases in average AF9 and ENL association with TSSs of most human genes in the same infected cells expressing DM-E1A, demonstrating the specificity of this effect on SEC subunit association at the viral early promoters (Figure 2c).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The ChIP-seq counts for AF9 and ENL in cells expressing wt E1A were twofold to fourfold higher at the E3 promoter compared to the E2early and E4 promoters.
source: The ChIP-seq counts for AF9 and ENL in cells expressing wt E1A were twofold to fourfold higher at the E3 promoter compared to the E2early and E4 promoters.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: In cells expressing DM-E1A, the ChIP-seq signals for AF9 and ENL at the E2early and E4 promoters were virtually eliminated, but clear peaks for AF9 and ENL persisted at the E3 promoter region, although they were reduced considerably compared to cells expressing wt E1A.
source: In cells expressing the DM-E1A, which caused hypoacetylation of H3K18/27 at the early viral promoters, the ChIP-seq signals for AF9 and ENL at the E2early and E4 promoters were virtually eliminated, but clear peaks for AF9 and ENL persisted at the E3 promoter region, although they were reduced considerably compared to cells expressing wt E1A (Figure 1, Figure 2b; Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 1 and 2b.

claim: BRD4 association at the E2early, E3, and E4 TSSs changed very little in cells infected with the DM-E1A vector compared to the wt E1A vector, although it was reduced to about 50% the level with wt E1A within the transcription units.
source: BRD4 association at the E2early, E3, and E4 TSSs changed very little in cells infected with the DM-E1A vector compared to the wt E1A vector, although it was reduced to about 50% the level with wt E1A within the transcription units (Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Association of the wt E1A-AD with CBP/p300 and the resulting acetylation of H3K18/27 in the early promoter regions are required for maximal recruitment of the SEC to the viral early promoters.
source: These data suggest that association of the wt E1A-AD with CBP/p300 and the resulting acetylation of H3K18/27 in the early promoter regions are required for maximal recruitment of the SEC to the viral early promoters.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the ChIP-seq data showing reduced SEC recruitment with DM-E1A.

claim: A-485 is a potent and specific small molecule inhibitor of CBP/p300 acetyl transferase activity that competes with acetyl-CoA for binding to the acetyl transferase domain active site.
source: A-485 is a potent and specific small molecule inhibitor of CBP/p300 acetyl transferase activity that competes with acetyl-CoA for binding to the acetyl transferase domain active site (Lasko et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A-485 treatment decreased total cell H3K18ac in HBTECs as confirmed by western blot.
source: Decreased total cell H3K18ac after A-485 treatment in HBTECs was confirmed by western blot (Figure 3a).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3a.

claim: ChIP-seq demonstrated A-485 inhibition of H3K18/27ac at viral early promoters, while H3K9ac was modestly affected.
source: ChIP-seq for H3K9ac, H3K18ac, and H3K27ac in wt E1A vector-infected cells treated with A-485 for 2 hr demonstrated A-485 inhibition of H3K18/27ac, as expected (Lasko et al., 2017; Weinert et al., 2018), while H3K9ac was modestly affected at viral early promoters (Figure 3b).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3b and citations to prior literature.

claim: Significant decreases in E2early and E4 pre-mRNA were observed after A-485 treatment, while E3 pre-mRNA was not decreased significantly.
source: We observed significant decreases in E2early and E4 pre-mRNA after A-485 treatment, while E3 pre-mRNA was not decreased significantly (Figure 3c).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The result that E3 transcription is less dependent on promoter H3K18/27ac than E2early and E4 transcription is confirmed by A-485 treatment.
source: This result confirms that E3 transcription is less dependent on promoter H3K18/27ac than E2early and E4 transcription (Hsu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the qRT-PCR data and citation to prior work.

claim: There was little difference in pausing index with A-485 treatment at the E2early (DMSO PI = 0.13, A-485 PI = 0.12) or E3 (DMSO PI = 1.20, A-485 PI = 1.19) promoters, but a clear increase in PI was observed for E4 (DMSO PI = 0.79, A-485 PI = 1.13).
source: There was little difference in PI with A-485 treatment at the E2early (DMSO (dimethyl sulfoxide) PI = 0.13, A-485 PI = 0.12) or E3 (DMSO (dimethyl sulfoxide) PI = 1.20, A-485 PI = 1.19) promoters, but a clear increase in PI was observed for E4 (DMSO (dimethyl sulfoxide) PI = 0.79, A-485 PI = 1.13) (Figure 4b).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRO-seq data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Release of paused Pol2 in the E4 promoter-proximal region depends on CBP/p300 HAT activity and is consistent with a requirement for promoter H3K18/27 acetylation for maximal E4 elongation.
source: These results indicate that release of paused Pol2 in the E4 promoter-proximal region depends on CBP/p300 HAT activity and is consistent with a requirement for promoter H3K18/27 acetylation for maximal E4 elongation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the GRO-seq data after A-485 treatment.

claim: A-485 treatment greatly decreased AF9 association at the E2early, E3, and E4 promoter regions.
source: As with cells expressing DM-E1A, A-485 treatment greatly decreased AF9 association at the E2early, E3, and E4 promoter regions, and decreased total ENL ChIP-seq counts from the E2early TTS to the right end of the genome from 13,712,875 to 10,804,279 reads, an ~20% decrease (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: A-485 treatment decreased total ENL ChIP-seq counts from the E2early TTS to the right end of the genome from 13,712,875 to 10,804,279 reads, an approximately 20% decrease.
source: As with cells expressing DM-E1A, A-485 treatment greatly decreased AF9 association at the E2early, E3, and E4 promoter regions, and decreased total ENL ChIP-seq counts from the E2early TTS to the right end of the genome from 13,712,875 to 10,804,279 reads, an ~20% decrease (Figure 4a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Decreased BRD4 was observed throughout the transcribed early regions in A-485-treated cells.
source: We also observed decreased BRD4 throughout the transcribed early regions in A-485-treated cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: Maximal recruitment of SEC complexes to viral early promoters requires H3K18/27ac by the CBP/p300 acetyl transferase catalytic domain targeted to the promoter region by the interaction between CBP/p300 and the E1A-AD acidic regions.
source: Taken together, these data show that maximal recruitment of SEC complexes to viral early promoters requires H3K18/27ac by the CBP/p300 acetyl transferase catalytic domain targeted to the promoter region by the interaction between CBP/p300 and the E1A-AD acidic regions (Figure 4c).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined ChIP-seq and GRO-seq data.

claim: Western blotting demonstrated an extensive decrease in total cellular H3K18ac, which approached steady state by 2 hr after addition of A-485.
source: Western blotting demonstrated an extensive decrease in total cellular H3K18ac, which approached steady state by 2 hr after addition of A-485, as expected (Lasko et al., 2017; Weinert et al., 2018; Figure 3a).
evidence: This claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3a and citations to prior literature.

claim: On average, A-485 caused greater decreases in both H3K18ac and H3K27ac at super-enhancers than typical enhancers.
source: Comparing the average signals for H3K18ac and H3K27ac, we observed the expected decreases due to A-485 treatment at both typical and super-enhancers (Figure 5a). But, on average, A-485 caused greater decreases in both H3K18ac and H3K27ac at super-enhancers than typical enhancers (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The pattern of greater decreases at super-enhancers than typical enhancers was also true for H3K9ac, although the hypoacetylation by A-485 was to a much lesser extent.
source: This pattern was also true for H3K9ac, although the hypoacetylation by A-485 was to a much lesser extent (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: An unexpected result was the increase in the average level of H3K18ac and H3K27ac at all TSSs in cells treated with A-485.
source: An unexpected result was the increase in the average level of H3K18ac and H3K27ac at all TSSs in cells treated with A-485 (Figure 5a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The percentage of total H3K27ac and H3K18ac peaks increased at promoters and decreased at enhancers after A-485 treatment, while the effects on H3K9ac peaks were minimal.
source: Furthermore, the percentage of total H3K27ac and H3K18ac peaks increased at promoters and decreased at enhancers after A-485 treatment, while the effects on H3K9ac peaks were minimal (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Homeostatic mechanisms function to maintain H3K18/27ac at promoters when CBP/p300, the principal cellular acetyl transferases for these sites, are extensively inhibited.
source: These observations indicate that homeostatic mechanisms function to maintain H3K18/27ac at promoters when CBP/p300, the principal cellular acetyl transferases for these sites (Weinert et al., 2018; Horwitz et al., 2008; Ferrari et al., 2014), are extensively inhibited.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the ChIP-seq data and citations to prior literature.

claim: Out of 10,062 active protein-coding genes, 686 (6.8%) had defective pause release after A-485 treatment (greater than twofold increase in PI, referred to as '2XPI' genes).
source: Out of 10,062 such active protein-coding genes, we found 686 (6.8%) with defective pause release after A-485 treatment (greater than twofold increase in PI, referred to as '2XPI' genes).
evidence: This claim is supported by genome-wide GRO-seq data analysis.

claim: 885 genes (8.8% of active genes) were inhibited for initiation (<50% the GRO-seq counts in the promoter region compared to control DMSO-treated cells), referred to as '2XIn' genes.
source: In total, 885 genes (8.8% of active genes) were inhibited for initiation (<50% the GRO-seq counts in the promoter region [TSS – 200 bp] compared to control DMSO-treated cells). We refer to these genes as '2XIn' genes for twofold decreased initiation from A-485.
evidence: This claim is supported by genome-wide GRO-seq data analysis.

claim: 217 genes passed the criteria for both 2XPI and 2XIn groups, indicating that both transcription initiation and promoter-proximal pause release were reduced by A-485 treatment for this small set of genes (approximately 2.15% of active genes).
source: Also, 217 genes passed the criteria for both groups, indicating that both transcription initiation and promoter-proximal pause release were reduced by A-485 treatment for this small set of genes (~2.15% of active genes, Figure 5b).
evidence: This claim is supported by genome-wide GRO-seq data analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of 2XPI genes revealed enrichment of genes involved in the development of multiple tissues, which is typical of genes regulated by enhancers.
source: Gene ontology analysis of 2XPI genes (Figure 5—figure supplement 3) revealed enrichment of genes involved in the development of multiple tissues (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), which is typical of genes regulated by enhancers (Bulger and Groudine, 2011; Levine, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3 and citations to prior literature.

claim: Both 2XPI and 2XIn genes were significantly closer to super-enhancers than randomly selected genes.
source: We found that, indeed, both 2XPI and 2XIn genes were significantly closer to super-enhancers than randomly selected genes (Figure 5c).
evidence: This claim is supported by distance analysis shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Super-enhancer-associated genes are more dependent on H3K18/K27ac for transcription initiation and elongation than the average expressed gene.
source: This suggests that super-enhancer-associated genes are more dependent on H3K18/K27ac for transcription initiation and elongation than the average expressed gene.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the distance analysis data.

claim: H3K18ac and K27ac at TSSs for 2XPI and 2XIn genes decreased in response to A-485, in contrast to the increase in H3K18 and K27 acetylation on average near the TSSs for all active genes in response to A-485.
source: H3K18ac and K27ac at TSSs for 2XPI and 2XIn genes decreased in response to A-485, as expected for a specific competitive inhibitor of the CBP/p300 acetyl transferase. But this was in contrast to the surprising increase in H3K18 and K27 acetylation on average near the TSSs for all active genes in response to A-485.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: H3K9ac did not change at the TSS in the average plot for all active genes or 2XPI genes after A-485 treatment, but did decrease for 2XIn genes.
source: In contrast, H3K9ac did not change at the TSS in the average plot for all active genes or 2XPI genes after A-485 treatment, but did decrease for 2XIn genes (Figure 6a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: H3K9ac may be sufficient for initiation but not elongation of genes with promoter H3K18/27 hypoacetylation.
source: This suggests that H3K9ac may be sufficient for initiation but not elongation of genes with promoter H3K18/27 hypoacetylation.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential effects of A-485 on H3K9ac at 2XPI versus 2XIn genes.

claim: AF9 and ENL were extensively enriched at TSSs and throughout gene bodies of 2XPI genes compared to the average for all active genes.
source: Remarkably, AF9 and ENL were extensively enriched at TSSs and throughout gene bodies of 2XPI genes compared to the average for all active genes.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: After A-485 treatment, AF9 and ENL association with 2XPI genes fell to the average level for all genes, which did not change with A-485 treatment.
source: Further, after A-485 treatment, AF9 and ENL association with 2XPI genes fell to the average level for all genes, which did not change with A-485 treatment.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Genes with an increase in PI after A-485 treatment (2XPI genes) had a very high association of SEC complexes throughout their transcription units that was selectively sensitive to A-485 treatment.
source: Thus, genes with an increase in PI after A-485 treatment (2XPI genes) had a very high association of SEC complexes throughout their transcription units that was selectively sensitive to A-485 treatment.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the ChIP-seq data for AF9 and ENL.

claim: Enrichment of AF9 and ENL was found at TSSs and throughout gene bodies in 2XIn genes, which fell to the level of the average for all genes after A-485 treatment.
source: Similarly, we found enrichment of AF9 and ENL at TSSs and throughout gene bodies in 2XIn genes, which fell to the level of the average for all genes after A-485 treatment (Figure 6c, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6c and Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: BRD4 association at the TSSs of all active genes was increased with A-485, while association near the TSS of 2XPI and 2XIn genes was reduced by A-485, but to a far less extent than the decrease in AF9 and ENL.
source: BRD4 association at the TSSs of all active genes was increased with A-485, while association near the TSS of 2XPI and 2XIn genes was reduced by A-485, but to a far less extent than the decrease in AF9 and ENL.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: Fifty-six percent of identified BRD4 peaks were >2.5 kb from the nearest TSS in control cells treated with DMSO.
source: Fifty-six percent of identified BRD4 peaks (see Materials and methods) were >2.5 kb from the nearest TSS in control cells treated with DMSO (dimethyl sulfoxide).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of BRD4 ChIP-seq data.

claim: Of BRD4 peaks >2.5 kb from the nearest TSS, 84% overlapped with peaks of H3K27ac, indicating that these peaks were primarily at enhancers.
source: Of these distal peaks, 84% overlapped with peaks of H3K27ac, indicating that these peaks were primarily at enhancers.
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of BRD4 and H3K27ac ChIP-seq data.

claim: There were 7554 BRD4 enhancer peaks where BRD4 decreased to <50% of control after A-485 treatment and 6324 peaks where BRD4 association remained unaltered or was not reduced to <50% of control.
source: There were 7554 peaks where BRD4 decreased to <50% of control after A-485 treatment and 6324 peaks where BRD4 association remained unaltered or was not reduced to <50% of control (referred to as A-485-sensitive and -resistant BRD4 enhancer peaks, respectively; Figure 7).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis of BRD4 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7.

claim: At both A-485-resistant and -sensitive BRD4 enhancer peaks, H3K18/27ac decreased following A-485 treatment.
source: At both A-485-resistant and -sensitive BRD4 enhancer peaks, H3K18/27ac decreased following A-485 treatment (Figure 7a).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: H3K9ac decreased only at the A-485-sensitive BRD4 peaks but not at A-485-resistant BRD4 peaks.
source: In contrast, H3K9ac decreased only at the A-485-sensitive BRD4 peaks but not at A-485-resistant BRD4 peaks.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: Enhancer H3K9ac correlates with BRD4 association and H3K9ac is sufficient for BRD4 association at enhancers.
source: These observations indicate that enhancer H3K9ac correlates with BRD4 association and suggest that H3K9ac is sufficient for BRD4 association at enhancers.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential effects of A-485 on H3K9ac and BRD4 at resistant versus sensitive enhancer peaks.

claim: A significant increase in PI distribution was observed for genes near A-485-sensitive BRD4 enhancer peaks compared to all active genes.
source: We observed a significant increase in PI distribution for genes near A-485-sensitive BRD4 acting at distal enhancers to stimulate transcription elongation of target genes (Kanno et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by analysis shown in Figure 7c.

claim: Histone H3 N-terminal tail acetylation in the promoter-proximal region regulates Pol2 release from promoter-proximal pause sites in a subset (approximately 4.3%) of active cellular promoters in primary human airway epithelial cells.
source: In addition to regulating PIC assembly and Pol2 initiation, our results support a mechanism by which histone H3 N-terminal tail acetylation in the promoter-proximal region regulates Pol2 release from promoter-proximal pause sites in a subset (~4.3%) of active cellular promoters in primary human airway epithelial cells.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the genome-wide data analysis.

claim: SEC recruitment through association with promoter region histone H3 acetylated at K18 and K27 stimulates paused Pol2 release at the HAdV-5 E4 promoter.
source: Initially we observed that SEC recruitment through association with promoter region histone H3 acetylated at K18 and K27 stimulates paused Pol2 release at the HAdV-5 E4 promoter (Figure 1a, Figure 2b).
evidence: This claim is supported by GRO-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 1a and 2b.

claim: The difference in the effects of A-485 on the rates of promoter versus enhancer acetylation by CBP/p300 is probably due to a faster average rate of H3K18/27 acetylation by CBP/p300 at promoters than at enhancers.
source: Consequently, the resistance of promoters to A-485-induced hypoacetylation compared to enhancers in living cells probably is a result of a faster average rate of H3K18/27 acetylation by CBP/p300 at promoters than at enhancers.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the differential effects of A-485 at promoters versus enhancers.

claim: The faster rate of H3K18/27 acetylation at promoters is the result expected if transient interactions between the ADs of activators bound to their cognate DNA-binding sites in enhancers increase the local concentration of CBP/p300 in promoter regions.
source: This is the result expected if transient interactions between the ADs of activators bound to their cognate DNA-binding sites in enhancers increase the local concentration of CBP/p300 in promoter regions.
evidence: This claim is based on speculation about the mechanism underlying the observed differential effects.

claim: BRD4 contains two bromodomains that bind acetylated lysines.
source: BRD4 contains two bromodomains that bind acetylated lysines (Filippakopoulos et al., 2012; Kanno et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The C-terminal portion of BRD4 binds P-TEFb and is thought to recruit it to hyperacetylated genomic regions to stimulate elongation.
source: The C-terminal portion of BRD4 binds P-TEFb and is thought to recruit it to hyperacetylated genomic regions to stimulate elongation (Chen et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: BRD4 has been shown to associate with promoters and enhancers and act as a histone chaperone to facilitate Pol2 elongation through chromatin to produce both protein-coding and enhancer RNAs.
source: BRD4 has been shown to associate with promoters and enhancers and act as a histone chaperone to facilitate Pol2 elongation through chromatin to produce both protein-coding and enhancer RNAs (Kanno et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: H3K9ac is sufficient for BRD4 recruitment at enhancers in the absence of H3K18/27ac.
source: By clustering BRD4 enhancer peaks into A-485-sensitive and A-485-resistant groups and correlating these peaks with H3K9ac and H3K18/27ac ChIP-seq data, we conclude that H3K9ac is sufficient for BRD4 recruitment at enhancers in the absence of H3K18/27ac (Figure 7a).
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7a.

claim: GRO-seq revealed a correlation between decreased BRD4 enhancer association and defective release of paused Pol2 from nearby promoters.
source: Additionally, GRO-seq in cells treated with A-485 revealed a correlation between decreased BRD4 enhancer association and defective release of paused Pol2 from nearby promoters.
evidence: This claim is supported by GRO-seq and ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: The mechanism by which BRD4 enhancer association affects Pol2 pause release is likely through direct promoter–enhancer interactions facilitated by long-range chromatin interactions.
source: The mechanism by which this occurs is likely through direct promoter–enhancer interactions facilitated by long-range chromatin interactions (Takahashi et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is based on speculation supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Another possibility is that transcription of enhancer RNAs facilitated by BRD4 stimulates paused Pol2 release by promoting NELF release at a promoter brought into close proximity to the enhancer by folding of the chromatin fiber.
source: Another possibility is that transcription of enhancer RNAs facilitated by BRD4 stimulates paused Pol2 release by promoting NELF release at a promoter brought into close proximity to the enhancer by folding of the chromatin fiber (Schaukowitch et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on speculation supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A consensus TATA box (TATAWAWR) in the promoter regions of cellular genes correlated with increased pausing for 2XPI genes and decreased initiation for 2XIn genes in response to A-485.
source: A consensus TATA box (TATAWAWR) in the promoter regions of cellular genes correlated with increased pausing for 2XPI genes and decreased initiation for 2XIn genes in response to A-485 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: TATA boxes are common in promoters of tightly regulated genes with focused TSSs, while TATA-less CpG island promoters are more common for constitutively expressed housekeeping genes with many unfocused TSSs.
source: TATA boxes are common in promoters of tightly regulated genes with focused TSSs, while TATA-less CpG island promoters are more common for constitutively expressed housekeeping genes with many unfocused TSSs (Juven-Gershon and Kadonaga, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Since 2XPI and 2XIn genes are enriched for developmental functions with tightly regulated expression, enrichment for TATA boxes in the promoters of these genes is expected.
source: Since 2XPI and 2XIn genes are enriched for developmental functions with tightly regulated expression, enrichment for TATA boxes in the promoters of these genes is expected.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the gene ontology and motif analysis data.

claim: The tightly regulated genes are dependent on the dynamic enhancer H3K18/27ac for either transcription initiation, elongation, or both.
source: This fits with the model that these tightly regulated genes are dependent on the dynamic enhancer H3K18/27ac for either transcription initiation, elongation, or both.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from the combined data analysis.
